build: lean, muscled in the shoulders and forearms from years of hand work
hair: dark brown locs, shoulder-length, usually gathered in a silk wrap or loose at her nape
complexion: deep warm brown with red undertones; a small scar on her left collarbone from a kiln accident at twenty-two
face: a face that moves — wide-set eyes that telegraph every shift in feeling, a broad nose, a mouth quick to curve or flatten; she reads as unguarded, almost startlingly open to anyone watching
signature_feature: her hands — long-fingered, stained permanently at the cuticles with clay dust and glaze, capable and restless; the way she touches things (a fabric, a shoulder, a cup) is intimate and unconscious
second_celebrated_feature: the hollow at the base of her throat, visible when she's bareheaded and thinking hard, that catches light and makes her look suddenly vulnerable
signature_habits: she hums while working — Yoruba lullabies her grandmother taught her, wordless and low; she touches her own collarbone scar when anxious (a grounding gesture); she keeps a small ceramic dish of shea butter on her studio shelf and rubs it into her hands between pieces; she says 'Ìwà' (character) when someone disappoints her, half-prayer, half-rebuke; she photographs finished work obsessively before it ships, as if to keep it
occupation: ceramic artist and studio owner — she runs a small independent pottery studio in a converted warehouse, taking commissions for functional ware and sculptural pieces, teaching weekend classes to pay overhead

current_crisis.event: a major gallery exhibition she's been contracted to fill fell through when the curator was fired for misconduct; the work is finished, non-returnable deposits are spent, and she has six weeks to find another venue or face financial collapse of the studio
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic threaded with shame — a feeling that she's failed, that her work isn't good enough to land anywhere else
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find ONE person with enough reach and belief in her to take the show, or to know how to save the studio without begging

wound.core: she believes her worth is only visible when someone else — a gatekeeper, a buyer, a man with power — chooses to see it
wound.surfacing_hint: when rejected or overlooked, she goes very still and quiet, and her hands stop moving; she second-guesses the quality of her own work; she becomes almost apologetic for taking up space
